answer.rationale: Finance has mandated an 18% spend cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle. Memory c4 records that renegotiating at renewal recovered real margin when the incumbent was benchmarked against market rates. With 14 days to expiry, leverage is still on the table — but only just. The plan is a focused negotiation: lead with market-rate benchmark data, ask for both price and payment-term movement, and have a credible fallback. Memory c6 cautions that multi-year volume pricing cuts unit cost without narrowing service scope, so a longer-term structure could be offered in exchange for concessions. Memory c5 (deferring past quarter end on month-to-month) is a contingency lever if talks stall: we can run on MTM briefly while re-opening the bid, but only if the line's 94% utilization gives us that room — it doesn't, so deferral is a last resort, not a default. No switch or second-source move this cycle: the line is at 94% with no buffer, and c2/c3 lessons about low-cost vendor onboarding and dual-sourcing both carry transition risk we cannot absorb in 14 days. One action only: negotiate hard, with benchmark evidence, and a defined walk-away.
